cues.text: Pinning means getting close to a customer. Do it safely and politely, so they feel comfortable.
The customer changes in the fitting room, never in the open shop.
Tell them what you will do before you touch the garment, like: I will pin the hem now.
Pins always point away from skin, and across the fabric, never straight in.
Use fine pins or chalk on silk, satin, and delicate fabric. Big pins leave holes.
Take pins from the pin cushion and count them, so none are left on the floor.
When they take it off, say: careful, there are pins inside. Offer to help with the jacket.
After pinning, keep the pins in. Fold it gently, put it in a bag with the ticket, and put it straight in the tailor bin. Never unpin a pinned garment.
